Paper Eq. (16): for positive score rᵢ and negative scores rⱼ, sⱼ=exp(rⱼ)/Σₖexp(rₖ), and L=−log(Σⱼsⱼσ(rᵢ−rⱼ))+λΣⱼsⱼrⱼ². This is the log of a weighted sigmoid sum, not a weighted sum of log-sigmoids. Score regularization penalizes squared negative scores, weighted by the same differentiable softmax; λ is `bpreg`, distinct from parameter weight decay. Implementations add 1e−24 inside the logarithm. No additional division by negative count. [Paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf)

Official PyTorch sampling concatenates the minibatch’s next-item targets with one shared vector of `n_sample` additional draws, sampled independently with replacement using q(item)∝training interaction count^`sample_alpha`; α=0 is uniform, α=1 popularity sampling. Each row excludes only its own diagonal target column. Reading the code: duplicate negative IDs remain separate columns; copies of the positive elsewhere also remain negatives. There is no item-identity deduplication, positive-collision rejection, or history exclusion. BPR-max applies ELU to affine output scores when `elu_param`>0: f(x)=x for x≥0, α(exp(x)−1) otherwise; nonpositive `elu_param` selects linear scores. Its negative softmax supplies loss weights, not output probabilities; `logq` is unused for BPR-max. [Official PyTorch source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py)

Both official implementations sum per-row losses and divide by configured `batch_size`, including when fewer sessions remain; this equals a batch mean only for full batches. Original Theano exposes additional final activations; its README recommends ELU-0.5 or ELU-1 for BPR-max. [Theano source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/master/gru4rec.py), [README](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/blob/master/README.md)
